title: Shadow-mode evaluation
summary: Compare Jev with reviewed outcomes and simpler credible alternatives.

sections.label: Experiment
items: Select a narrow task such as holiday scope-support checking.
Build reviewed positive, negative, ambiguous, and conflicting examples.
Run Jev without changing publication behavior.
Compare existing rules, a constrained utility LLM, and the current reviewer process.
Measure missed errors, false alarms, review effort, cost, and language differences.
Decide whether benefits justify integration and which cases need escalation.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Improvement is demonstrated on held-out cases. The model and question versions are recorded and changes trigger re-evaluation.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended use: Use the existing experiment-plan mapping to compare proposed judgments without changing publication behavior.
Reserve comparison cases that were not used to tune the question or threshold.
Prove the trial has no live publication effect and retain reviewer labels and disagreement.
Workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Existing examples, tenant availability, older product claims and comparative benefits were not revalidated by this mapping review.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Anthropic distinguishes task criteria, repeated trials, grading and the final environment outcome, and recommends inspecting results beyond an agent's success claim. This scoped source fact was checked on 15 October 2026. The guide's broader workflow and examples remain Atlas proposals, not demonstrated outcomes.

catalog.applicability: Use this Jev example when you want to test Jev on a narrow task, such as holiday scope-support checking, without changing publication behavior. Compare it with existing rules, a constrained utility LLM and the current reviewer process on reviewed examples, and record the model and question versions.
